sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Wholesale Brokerage of Marine Fuel Oil and Distillates

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of Panama (Unitary National Jurisdiction, Municipality of Panama registry office)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified commercial law; Private Interest Foundation regime draws upon common-law trust concepts and equitable fiduciary principles; unified national regulation without sub-state corporate law distinctions)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Treaty Concerning the Treatment and Protection of Investments (1982, in force 1991)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (as amended by Law 11 of 2010 and Law 41 of 2013); Law 23 of 27 April 2015 on AML/CFT (as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Law 254 of 2019); Executive Decree 128 of 18 February 2011 (CDD); Law 129 of 30 September 2020 (Final Beneficiary Register, operated by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)); Law 38 of 2000 (Administrative Procedure); note: Panama has been under FATF heightened monitoring since 28 June 2024.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of the founder and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the document holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing country) OR Consular Legalization (Panamanian consulate in the issuing country for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and recent statement for the founder's funding bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank holding the founder's transaction account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by a Panama Notary Public (for foreign-issued letters, apostille or consular legalization applies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Incumbency of any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the corporate founder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted to the Panamanian resident agent / incorporation attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, followed by certified Spanish translation in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth and source of funds declaration (declaración jurada) for the founding endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder and law firm preparing the foundation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a Panamanian Notary Public (authenticated documents from abroad require apostille/consular legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) for the DGI Final Beneficiary Register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Resident agent filing with Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal government filing; no apostille required; supporting identity documents require standard notarization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of the founder, protector, foundation council members, beneficiaries, and all counterparties (including charterer/bunker supplier chains) against: United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN) and sectoral sanctions list (SSI); United Nations Security Council Consolidated List (ISIL/Al-Qaida 1267/1989, DPRK 1718, Iran 2231); European Union consolidated financial sanctions database; United Kingdom OFSI consolidated list; BIS Entity List for export controls on dual-use fuels; Panamanian UAF national terrorist list; and the DGI/Bloomberg/World-Check enhanced PEP database. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any Politically Exposed Person (Law 23 of 2015, Article 12) with continued monitoring for at least 12 months after separation from public office; beneficial ownership is verified to the 10% ownership/control threshold with specific identification of control through the Foundation Council and protector positions. Given the 28 June 2024 FATF increased monitoring designation, all foreign-source documents require apostille, independent verification, and translation, and all wire funding of the foundation endowment must be traced to the originator bank account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Sistema de Registro en Línea (Online Registration System, https://www.registropublico.gob.pa), Foundations Registry Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name may be expressed in Spanish or in any foreign language, but must contain the Spanish term 'Fundación' (Law 25 of 1995, Article 5); names in non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK ideograms) must be transliterated into Latin-alphabet characters and, where necessary, accompanied by a Spanish translation; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already inscribed in the Public Registry, evaluated according to the Registry's phonetic and literal confusion doctrine.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Banco', 'Financiera', 'Banca' (requires prior license/authorization from Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá)
'Seguro', 'Aseguradora', 'Reaseguradora' (requires prior authorization from Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros)
'Valores', 'Casa de Valores', 'Fondo de Inversión', 'Bolsa' (requires prior authorization from Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores)
'Gobierno', 'Ministerio', 'Nacional', 'Oficial', 'Público', 'Estado', 'Policía', 'Ejército' (suggestions of official or governmental connection, prohibited without ministerial sanction)
'Cruz Roja', 'Seguro Social', 'Caja de Ahorros' (protected institutional designations)
'Petróleo', 'Hidrocarburo', 'Combustible', 'Energía', 'Bunker' (triggers mandatory consultation with the Secretaría Nacional de Energía because of the ISIC 4661 petroleum wholesale business)
Names identical or phonetically equivalent to an already registered entity or foundation (absolute rejection ground)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name availability certificate (constancia de nombre) is valid for 30 calendar days during which the acta constitutiva must be presented; extension may be obtained by re-filing the search request before expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant (through the resident agent) files a written motion for reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) before the Director of the Foundations Registry within five (5) working days of notification, and a further administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) within five (5) working days to the General Directorate of the Public Registry under Law 38 of 2000, attaching a legal memorandum demonstrating absence of confusion and compliance with the 'Fundación' token requirement; a rejected name cannot be re-filed simultaneously, and a new application with a materially distinct name may be submitted in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-office arrangement is permissible for the foundation's registered address only where the designated resident agent (agente residente) maintains a physical, operational office in Panama at which statutory records, the foundation's accounts, and the confidential by-laws (reglamento) are kept available for inspection by DGI and UAF; for the active marine fuel brokerage activity, Law 254 of 2019 economic substance rules require actual presence (local office, local management, local employees) if the activity is characterized as a 'relevant activity', so pure virtualization without any physical substance in Panama would expose the PIF to economic-substance penalties and bank account termination.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated for the petroleum wholesale sector: estimated 35-45% probability of an unannounced visit within the first 18 months of operation, primarily triggered by Law 254/2019 economic substance compliance audits by DGI (random selection of high-risk taxpayers), UAF sectoral examinations of obliged entities, and the physical-address verification protocols applied by all Panamanian banks during the account-opening process for energy trading clients.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and certificate (constancia de búsqueda de nombre) in the Foundations Section
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff (arancel) as published by the Registro Público

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarization of the foundation charter (acta constitutiva) and confidential by-laws (reglamento), including Spanish-language compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm / notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for private interest foundation formation (US$850–US$1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry inscription fee (inscripción de la fundación) and official stamps (papel sellado y timbres)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff and fiscal stamp schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year resident agent fee (agente residente) including registered office address and statutory records custody
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Resident agent (licensed attorney or law firm)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial foundation endowment (patrimonio fundacional) — no statutory minimum, practical minimum recommended for bank account opening and bunker-trade credibility
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foundation bank account (escrow to be funded upon incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Founder's contribution; documented under Law 25 of 1995 Article 7 and verified by source-of-funds declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization of founder identity and corporate documents, plus certified Spanish translations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaría Pública de Panamá; Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (apostille/legalizations); certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariffs and apostille fees; market translator rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Final Beneficiary Register filing (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) with DGI under Law 129 of 2020
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing requirement; DGI administrative fee and professional preparation charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal operating notice (Aviso de Operación) for wholesale brokerage activities in Panama City
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Municipal tariff calculated on declared capital and activity classification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hydrocarbon wholesale/brokering permit application fee (licencia o registro de comercializador de hidrocarburos) before the Secretaría Nacional de Energía, including legal opinion on the bunker-fuel regulatory scope
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under hydrocarbon regulations; professional legal drafting benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance package: AML manual, risk-based assessment, compliance officer appointment, PEP and sanctions screening setup, and UAF-required internal procedures for a High_Risk_Special_License activity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML compliance consultancy / appointed compliance officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for high-risk commodity trading AML programs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Anti-corruption and tax red-flag review of proposed counterparties (bunker suppliers, charterers) — Stage 1 adverse media and OFAC/UN screening reports
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/sanctions screening platform (World-Check / OFAC API) and counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for commercial database subscriptions and analytical legal review

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (as amended by Law No. 10 of 2020), Articles 6-15, 18, 24 and 40; Executive Decree 473 of 2021 on Beneficial Ownership; residence-agent requirements under the Regulation of the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Publico de Panama (Public Registry of Panama) - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Publica Constitutiva de Fundacion de Interes Privado (Notarized Public Deed of Incorporation of a Private Interest Foundation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum endowment under Law 25 of 1995; a declared and vested amount of at least USD 10,000 is conventionally documented in the deed. Escrow is not legally mandated; the Settlor's contribution is certified in the notarial record and acknowledged as fully paid into the Foundation's patrimony.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION: RESOLVED that the initial endowment of USD 10,000 declared by the Settlor is accepted and assigned to the Foundation's patrimony, recorded and receipted as fully vested; RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office at Calle 50, Marbella, Panama City, is ratified as the Foundation's legal seat; RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be and is hereby appointed President, [Name] Treasurer, and [Name] Secretary of the Foundation Council; RESOLVED FURTHER that the President, jointly with the Treasurer, is authorized to execute trading and bank-account documents for wholesale marine-fuel brokerage, and to retain a licensed natural or legal person operator for regulated fuel marketing; RESOLVED FINALLY that the Resident Agent is authorized to file fees and registry updates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Online Name Reservation Portal (Ventanilla Electronica) and Panamanian Counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online name-reservation petition with the Public Registry portal. Upon approval, instruct a licensed Panamanian attorney to draft the Foundation Charter (Escritura Publica) including the purpose clause for wholesale marine-fuel brokerage, Foundation Council rules, and appointment of a Resident Agent. Use the Separate Statement of Appointment to keep the Settlor and Council members confidential in the public deed.
required_dossiers: Notarized identity document of the Settlor/Founder
Certified corporate existence and good standing certificate of founder (if corporate settlor)
Draft purpose and initial endowment charter clauses
Signed Resident Agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected due to similarity, file an administrative reconsideration with the Registry's Directorate General or resubmit using a second-choice name; a new reservation fee applies only to the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaria Publica (Notary Public) of Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian Notary Public. All signatories must present valid identification and pay notarial fees (approx. USD 50-150). The Notary authenticates signatures and, where elected, transcribes the Separate Statement of Appointment to shield officer identities from the public registry.
required_dossiers: Approved final charter draft
Passport or Cedula of the Settlor and Council members
Resident Agent service contract
Name reservation approval certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary raises observations on the purpose clause or asset clauses, amend the charter text and re-execute the deed; immaterial errors are corrected by an addendum (aclaracion) subscribed before the same Notary prior to registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed with the Public Registry within 15 days of execution. The Registry examines legality and form, issues observations (reparos) if any, and, upon satisfaction, inscribes the Foundation in the Private Interest Foundation Register. Pay the registration tariff (approx. USD 250) plus applicable municipal stamp duties.
required_dossiers: Original notarized foundation deed
Registry inscription fee payment receipt
Notary's certificacion de autentica (certificate of authenticity)
Power of attorney to the filing attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure any registry observations within 30 days by filing a written correction brief with the amended clause. If the Registry refuses registration, appeal to the Director General of the Public Registry, and subsequently to the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice as a final judicial remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Resident Agent Certification and Registry Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent (Panamanian licensed attorney) and Registro Publico de Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, obtain the Certified Copy of the Foundation Charter (Copia Certificada) and the Registry Certificate of Registration. The Resident Agent issues the formal certification of appointed officers and, upon request, obtains a Certificado de Personeria Juridica to support bank KYC and counterparty due diligence.
required_dossiers: Registry folio number (inscripcion)
Certified copy of the inscribed deed
Resident Agent engagement agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or transcript errors, file an erratum petition with the Public Registry; corrected duplicates are re-issued within 24 hours upon payment of the corresponding fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Registry Filing (Executive Decree 473 of 2021)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Registro de Beneficiario Final (integrated with the Direccion General de Ingresos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the initial beneficial-ownership return within 30 calendar days of registration, disclosing the Settlor and any person directly or indirectly holding 10% or more of the Foundation's patrimony or controlling the Council. Panamanian law requires the Resident Agent to file the return and to maintain accurate underlying records.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership declaration form
Legalized identity documents of each beneficial owner
Power of attorney authorizing the Resident Agent to file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing attracts scaled fines; file a corrective declaration with payment of the corresponding fine. Registry rejections may be cured by re-filing with corrected KYC data within five business days without prejudice to the penalty waiver application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaria Nacional de Energia de Panama - Direccion Nacional de Hidrocarburos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the pre-application for the wholesale commercialization license of refined petroleum products. Demonstrate technical competence, financial solvency, and terminal storage agreements. Because a Private Interest Foundation is a civil-purpose vehicle, the license shall be structured in the name of a Panama operating company (Sociedad Anonima) wholly held by the Foundation; the Foundation Council authorizes the equity participation and service contracts.
required_dossiers: Foundation charter and registry certificate
Certificate of good standing of the proposed operating company
Audited financial statements or bank solvency letter
Terminal storage contracts or ship supply agreements
AML/KYC compliance manual aligned with the High-Risk Special License tier
Lease or ownership title of the commercial office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Under the statutory tacit-approval rule, failure to decide within the legal term may be treated as approval only where expressly permitted; otherwise, file an administrative appeal within five business days of denial, heard by the superior body of the National Energy Secretariat, and thereafter before the Contentious-Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaria Nacional de Energia de Panama - Direccion Nacional de Hidrocarburos (with facilitation by Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias for mercantile permits)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso de Comercializacion Mayorista de Hidrocarburos - Productos Refinados (Wholesale Marketing Permit for Crude Oil and Refined Products) under Law 109 of 2013

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Direccion de Verificacion del Desempeno Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I - Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental) for pure wholesale brokerage offices without fuel storage; full EIA Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, Categoria III) required if storage, blending, or tanker operations exceed 10,000 barrels per month.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero-discharge policy for office operations; any oily wastewater effluent limited to 15 mg/L total petroleum hydrocarbons under Panama's national effluent standards; VOC emissions control through closed-loop sample handling; hazardous waste manifests must be filed with MiAMBIENTE for spent lubricants and fuel-contaminated rags; compliance with air emission thresholds per the national air quality regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama for the commercial office and any permitted fuel sampling area, renewable annually; structural load inspection certificate for any warehouse or dispensing premises; workplace safety clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) covering fire extinguishers, first-aid kits, fuel-handling training, and emergency evacuation plan; SINAPROC hazardous-materials advisory for any storage of diesel or marine gas oil samples.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama. Online portal: e-Tax (https://etax.mef.gob.pa); ancillary statistical filing via SIME.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Appoint a resident legal agent and, where required, a certified public accountant; 2) execute the Private Interest Foundation charter (escritura de fundación de interés privado) before a Panamanian notary and inscribe it at the Registro Público de Panamá under Ley 25 de 1995; 3) obtain the official foundation registration record (ficha) and certified copy of the charter; 4) file the RUC application with DGI using Form 3B (Solicitud de Inscripción de Persona Jurídica) through e-Tax, attaching the registered charter, ficha, identification of the Foundation Council member(s), and the resident agent's power of attorney; 5) DGI reviews declared Panamanian-source business activities and issues the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) with economic-activity codes covering wholesale trading in crude oil and refined products at ISIC 4661 / NAICS 424720; 6) after RUC issuance, file monthly ITBMS declaration Form 304 and the annual income tax return. Beneficiaries of the foundation need not be disclosed to the DGI unless they are Panamanian residents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope - Panama applies territorial taxation: income tax is levied solely on income derived from Panamanian sources. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Ley 25 de 1995 is a juridical person of a private, non-commercial nature, but may hold assets and perform contracts; income from offshore marine-fuel brokerage and any other foreign-source activity falls outside the Panamanian fiscal net. If the foundation conducts economic activities with Panamanian-source revenue, it is taxed at the standard corporate rate of 25% on taxable income, and ITBMS obligations attach to local supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available elections and special regimes: (1) territorial-source election - taxpayers may segregate Panamanian- and foreign-source income using the 'causa eficiente' (effective-cause) test and supporting economic-substance evidence; (2) small-taxpayer simplified regime under Law 256 of 2022 for gross annual turnover up to B/. 300,000, involving substitute monthly taxation; (3) Multinational Headquarters (SEM/EM) licence under Law 41 of 2007, as amended by Law 254 of 2022, with a reduced 5% effective income tax rate on qualifying intragroup service income; (4) Law 254 of 2022 anti-hybrid and economic-substance provisions requiring annual certification of real activity for foundations managing financial or trading operations from Panama; (5) bilateral treaty/APAs and MLI elective positions for double-tax relief. A purely patrimonial PIF may elect not to register a RUC at all, provided it generates no Panamanian-source commercial income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) - Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for commercial operators: any person or juridical entity habitually transferring movable goods or rendering services in Panamanian territory must register for ITBMS before commencing activities. A simplified 'Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente' exists for taxpayers with gross annual receipts up to B/. 300,000 under Law 256 of 2022; such taxpayers pay a substitute monthly tax and have restricted input-credit entitlements. Wholesale marine-fuel trading is normally conducted under the general ITBMS regime to preserve zero-rating credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing applies under DGI Resolution 266-2019 and amendments. Large taxpayers (Grandes Contribuyentes) were phased in from February 2021; the remaining registered economic operators became subject to mandatory electronic invoicing through 2022-2023. Every invoice must be transmitted in real time to the DGI Fiscal Invoicing System (Sistema de Facturación Fiscal) or issued through an authorized technological service provider; clearance is evidenced by the 52-character Código de Seguridad Fiscal (CSF) embedded in a QR code on the PDF representation. REST/JSON API integration with enterprise resource planning systems is accepted. Export and zero-rated invoices must cite the corresponding export/zero-rating code and be reconciled with the electronic customs declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS at 0% applies to (a) tangible goods physically exported from Panama under an accepted customs export declaration; (b) services supplied to non-residents where the effective use or exploitation occurs entirely outside Panama; and (c) the supply of marine fuel (bunkering) to vessels engaged in international navigation from Panamanian ports, evidenced by the International Bunker Delivery Note and the vessel's IMO certificate. For ISIC 4661 wholesale brokerage transactions in which title and risk pass outside Panamanian territory, the supply is outside the scope of ITBMS and no tax is due; zero-rating is claimed only when the sales invoice is issued from Panama and the export evidence bundle is maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas - DUA) with SISA system authorization stamp
Bill of Lading or sea waybill (mate's receipt acceptable for local-port bunkering)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT-103 / credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a US-dollar Panamanian bank account
IMO International Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) for marine fuel supplies
Certificate of origin or ISIC activity certificate supporting the export nature of the transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits zero-rated export claims through cross-verification of customs exit records, vendor/consignee identity, bill-of-lading dates, and inward remittance traceability. Failure to substantiate a zero-rated invoice triggers retrospective assessment of the 7% ITBMS with default interest, a recalculation surcharge of up to 100% of the omitted tax (Código Fiscal Article 760), and administrative fines ranging from 100% to 200% of the tax evaded. Fraudulent export zero-rating schemes constitute tax fraud (defraudación fiscal) under Código Fiscal Article 762, punishable by imprisonment from 2 to 5 years where the amount exceeds B/. 10,000, and may also trigger customs contraband penalties of up to ten times the commercial value of the goods under Ley 66 de 2014. For a Private Interest Foundation, such violations expose the foundation to RUC cancellation, personal liability of the Foundation Council members for breach of fiduciary duties, and mandatory reports by the Registro Público to the Public Prosecutor's Office.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP), the sole banking-prudential and AML/CFT supervisor under Decree Law 9 of 1998 and Law 23 of 2015; no conventional central bank and no separate foreign-exchange-administration agency exist in Panama. The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the state-owned Banco Nacional de Panamá perform fiscal-agent and domestic-clearing roles; monetary policy is de facto delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve because the U.S. dollar is full legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility under a complete dollarization regime (Law 84 of 1941; Decree Law 9 of 1998). There are no capital-account or current-account exchange controls, no IMF Article VIII restrictions, no prior-approval regime for profit remittance, dividend distribution, interest payment, or liquidation proceeds. A Panama Private Interest Foundation may hold, repatriate, and distribute funds in USD without central-bank authorization; the only practical impediments are individual-bank Enhanced Due Diligence, FATCA/CRS classification, and the need to maintain registered-agent, beneficial-ownership, and source-of-funds records. Territorial taxation applies exclusively to Panamanian-source income, so a non-resident PIF engaged in foreign trade incurs zero Panama withholding, but counterparty banks may require a provisional tax-residence and economic-substance letter to prevent CRS re-rating as a Reportable Account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export or trade receipts. Proceeds from wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and refined distillates (ISIC 4661) may be retained freely in U.S. dollars, held onshore or offshore, and re-deployed without clearance. The receiving bank treats the inflow as commercial turnover supported by the commercial invoice, bill of lading or bunker-delivery note, and broker confirmation; standard UAF/SBP transaction reporting applies only to cash and suspicious-activity thresholds, not to wire receipts. No declaration to the SBP or MEF is required for foreign-currency retention.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules_note: Blank field reserved for jurisdictions with surrender regimes; Panama has no such rule.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Panama does not maintain a standalone e-money-institution (EMI) license class, and Decree Law 9 of 1998 restricts deposit-taking, escrow, and payment-account services to licensed banks or SBP-authorized payment providers. U.S. or EU EMI licenses are not passportable into Panama. Cross-border digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, ConnectPay, Currencycloud) may be used only as ancillary collection gateways for small ticket invoices; they cannot issue or confirm Standby Letters of Credit, cannot support documentary trade clearing or SWIFT MT700 flows, and their inability to provide the USD correspondent backbone required for marine-fuel settlements makes them legally and operationally unsuitable as the primary treasury rail. Feasibility rating for the ISIC 4661 broker model: Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory for high-risk classifications. Under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Agreement 2-2013, an energy-trading Private Interest Foundation is deemed high-risk, requiring Enhanced Due Diligence. All tier-1 Panamanian banks require at least one in-person appearance: the ultimate beneficial owner or an appointed statutory director with a notarized and apostilled power of attorney must attend a face-to-face interview at the Panamanian branch in Panama City. Fully remote opening is not available for a marine-fuel brokerage PIF; preliminary video calls, notarized identification packets, and international bank references may precede, but never replace, the physical interview of the signatory. Practical blueprint: schedule a three-day Panama visit for the settlor and tax director, carrying the original foundation instrument, registered-agent certificate, source-of-wealth file, and a cover letter from the commercial bank expressing willingness to open the operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation opacity: nominee council, registered-agent-only structure, no direct ownership visibility
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or notarized Foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva) with a certified English translation; current beneficial-ownership declaration under Law 23 of 2015; resident-agent certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian law firm; register of council members and protector; notarized source-of-funds statement and opening balance-sheet evidencing the initial endowment; letter of economic purpose and intended trade activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure and adverse media in the marine-fuel supply chain (Venezuela, Russia, Iran, Syria, ship-to-ship transfer flags of convenience)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live OFAC/SDN, EU, UN, and UAF screening report dated within 24 hours of each transaction; written sanctions-compliance policy naming a designated compliance officer; certificate of product origin from the refinery or licensed supplier; vessel due-diligence file including IMO number, flag, ISM certificate, and AIS tracking log; Incoterms-defining master agreement; external legal opinion from Panamanian counsel confirming that the heavy fuel oil traded is not of embargoed origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth and source of funds for large USD capital injections and high-volume SBLC-backed receivables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month bank statements of the funding entity; notarized source-of-wealth questionnaire with independent auditor sign-off; parent-company financial statements or corporate tax filing; the signed funding or contribution resolution of the PIF council; for shareholder loans, a written intercompany loan agreement with amortization schedule and stated interest; evidence that tainted or anonymous funding is absent (e.g., open-bank confirmation).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade pattern: identical back-to-back commercial letters of credit, rapid conversion of SBLC draws into cash, multi-hop commission payments to third-country brokers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreement and matching on-sale contract; independent cargo survey certificate (SGS, Intertek or equivalent); bill of lading or bunker-delivery note; voyage-charter and freight invoice; structured broking commission agreement with anti-ghost-commission certification; internal AML compliance procedure with a Money-Laundering Prevention Officer; comprehensive transaction file for every MT103/MT700 clearing showing the end-to-end commercial chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP linkage of settlor, protector, or ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP declaration in the SBP standard form; independent source-of-wealth report prepared by a licensed external auditor; explicit refusal to accept any PEP-associated funding without an in-depth written opinion; complete ownership-chain disclosure to the ultimate natural person; written instructions from the foundation council and separate legal counsel confirming the economic substance of the settlor's participation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: CRS/FATCA re-rating as a Reportable Account due to the Foundation's hybrid legal classification and territorial tax treatment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS self-certification form (FATCA Form W-8BEN-E for non-US beneficial owners; Form W-9 where applicable); IRS GIIN registration match if the PIF is treated as a Panamanian Financial Institution; registered-agent confirmation and provisional non-resident tax status; corporate organizational chart proving no entity residence in a jurisdiction on the EU blacklist; contemporaneous record of registered office, minutes, and economic substance in Panama.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing uses the Foundation's own USD-denominated account at a tier-1 Panamanian bank, funded through a New York correspondent (Fedwire or CHIPS) via SWIFT MT103 with a structured remittance reference such as 'CAP/PA_PIF + folio number' and an underlying notarized capital-contribution deed or intercompany loan agreement. Because Panama operates no exchange-control registration and no purpose-code (BPM) classification regime, there is no central-bank declaration requirement; the receiving bank applies Know-Your-Transaction scrutiny requiring: (i) board or council resolution authorizing the inflow; (ii) source-of-funds confirmation with the contributing entity's bank statements; (iii) identification of the ultimate funder for any amount above USD 50,000; and (iv) OFAC/UAF screen-clear. For shareholder-loan injections, provide the signed loan agreement, interest-rate rationale, and repayment schedule; no withholding applies to capital injections or loan principal since the income is foreign-source for Panamanian territorial tax purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the marine-fuel wholesale model: (1) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for direct supplier, broker, surveyor, and freight payments; (2) SWIFT MT700/MT720 commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP600 for crude-oil and refined-product purchases against presentation of the commercial invoice, bill of lading, certificate of quality/quantity, and certificate of origin; (3) Standby Letters of Credit under ISP98 or URDG 758 issued by the Panamanian bank or transmitted through a confirming bank in Miami, New York, or Geneva as performance or payment collateral; (4) MT202/MT202COV for correspondent-only interbank settlement when clearing through an intermediary bank; (5) documentary collections (DP/DA) for mid-sized purchasers where LC cover is not cost-effective; and (6) internal liquidity sweeps between the foundation's capital-escrow and operational accounts. All disbursements above USD 25,000 require dual-signature (maker-checker), automated OFAC pre-screening, and a transaction file containing the sale/purchase contract, pro-forma invoice, Incoterms, and vessel or BDN evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX Forwards (USD/EUR, USD/COP, USD/MXN, USD/CLP, USD/PEN) executed through the Panamanian bank or an eligible international counterparty under an ISDA 2022 Master Agreement, provided the hedging tenor matches the cargo settlement cycle and is documented as a commercial hedge.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for Latin American currencies with restricted offshore delivery (e.g., COP, CLP, PYG) where the Panamanian bank nets settlement in USD without principal exchange.

Cross-currency basis swaps (USD against EUR or cargo-related currencies) permitted for aligning receivable and payable currency mixes on long-term supply contracts, subject to SBP risk-management suitability assessment.
European-style vanilla FX options for committed cargo obligations only, with plain vanilla premium payment, no speculative naked positions, and full ISDA/CSA collateral documentation.

mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial taxation system. Corporate income tax is levied only on net income derived from Panamanian-source activities. Qualifying income from international trading, marine fuel brokering, or export-oriented services may be exempt where title, risk, and execution occur outside Panama. PIFs are generally not subject to income tax unless they carry on commercial or industrial activities with Panamanian-source income. No statutory tax holidays apply to PIFs, but tax stability agreements may fix rates for up to 10 years for licensed logistics operators.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 301 (Declaración Anual de Renta) submitted electronically through the DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) online portal / T@PA system. Other forms: Form 308/309 for quarterly advance payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return is due within three months of the fiscal year end (typically March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers). Quarterly advance payments are due on March, June, September, and December; final settlement with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification and RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) number, fiscal period, and taxpayer type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF must obtain a RUC through its resident agent; file nil return if no Panamanian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian-source gross revenue from wholesale brokerage, commissions, and margin income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue effectively connected to a Panamanian permanent establishment or sourced via negotiation/execution in Panama. Offshore broker fees should be excluded with documentary support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: direct costs, brokerage commissions paid, demurrage, insurance, freight, and overheads related to Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs economically linked to taxable revenue are deductible. PIF must maintain contemporaneous contracts, invoices, and shipping evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (after deductions) for Panama-source activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panama-source activities, enter zero. For partial physical operations (e.g. bunkering in Panama waters), allocate revenue and costs carefully.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits for advanced payments, withholding taxes, and other allowable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits arise from Panama-source withholding (e.g. dividend or service payments) or quarterly prepayments. No foreign tax credit is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) calculation, where applicable, based on gross assets or gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs with Panamanian-source gross income exceeding thresholds may be subject to AMT if the ordinary tax is low. Assess eligibility with the local representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Education insurance surtax (2% of taxable income) and other national surtaxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payable only if the PIF has Panamanian-source taxable income. Otherwise, enter zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable / balance due after credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must settle balances electronically in USD. Ensure timely payment to avoid surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal representative and resident agent declaration, signature, and CPA certification if required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident agent or licensed accountant must e-sign. Power of attorney and entity records must confirm authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction, capped at 50% of the tax due. Minimum absolute fine of USD 100 up to USD 10,000. Late payment interest of 1% monthly. Failure to file nil returns may trigger administrative fines. Persistent non-compliance can lead to license suspension and exclusion from public tenders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends or other profit distributions paid by a Panama-domiciled entity to a non-resident beneficiary. Distributions from PIF to non-resident beneficiaries are generally outside Panama-source taxation unless attributed to Panama-source commercial activity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited DTA network. To claim treaty relief on dividends/royalties/interest, the non-resident must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from their country of residence, (ii) submit the TRC with apostille/legalization, (iii) provide a beneficial ownership declaration to the Panamanian withholding agent to reduce the rate or obtain a refund. For Panama-source dividends paid to a treaty resident, the DGI may require prior approval via a refund procedure if tax was over-withheld. Maintain all documentation for 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.5% statutory WHT on gross Panamanian-source royalties; treaty rates may reduce to 10% (depending on DTA). Interest: 12.5% statutory WHT on gross interest paid to non-residents (5% for bank or financial institution interest in certain cases). Treaty reductions may apply. No Panama WHT on offshore interest income earned by a PIF outside Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File) required when the taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds USD 10 million or related-party transactions exceed USD 2 million (thresholds in Panamanian Balboas / USD). Master File required for multinational groups meeting the revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has an economic substance framework through the Law 254 of 2019 and DGI regulations. A PIF engaged in trading or brokering must meet physical presence, employees, expenditure, and core income-generating activity tests. A PIF that is tax transparent or only holds assets must not derive unrestricted trading income without substance in Panama; otherwise, the PIF can be re-domiciled or sanctioned as a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting Panamanian-source income, overstating deductions, or documenting fake brokerage invoices through the PIF for oil trades.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 50% to 100% of the tax evaded, plus 1% monthly interest. Criminal tax fraud prosecuted under the Criminal Code: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and fines of USD 20,000 to USD 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, founder/council members, and resident agent may be held jointly liable if they signed false returns or knowingly assisted in fraud. Civil restitution, asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance Failure / Shell Company Allegation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a PIF with no office, staff, or activity in Panama to intermediate crude oil trades, while claiming tax residency in a low-tax region without business substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may levy administrative fines up to USD 25,000; the Superintendence of Non-Financial Entities may dissolve the PIF. The entity may be treated as a tax shell, losing the territorial tax benefit. For PIFs used in tax arbitrage, penalties of 50% of the omitted tax can be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: When directors and the protector (beneficial owner) direct the shell, authorities can pierce the veil: personal fines of USD 100,000, confiscation of profits, travel bans, and criminal prosecution for money laundering or tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling payments for sanctioned entities or vessels linked to prohibited countries; using SBLC (Standby Letters of Credit) and SWIFT wires to launder proceeds through a PIF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's AML Law (Law 23 of 2015) imposes fines of USD 100,000 to USD 1 million, criminal prosecution for money laundering (8 to 18 years' imprisonment), and mandatory reporting of suspicious transactions. Business license cancellation is a secondary sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal criminal liability: imprisonment 8 to 12 years for ordinary money laundering, 12 to 18 years for aggravated laundering. Directors may be extradited; travel bans and asset freezes are common.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not maintaining contemporaneous TP documentation for related-party commissions, fees, or financing structures with the PIF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% to 20% of the underpaid tax attributed to TP adjustments. Late documentation fines of USD 5,000 to USD 10,000 per category of missing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to ensure TP filing can be personally fined up to USD 10,000 and jointly liable for the underpaid tax if found negligent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in physical wholesale brokerage of crude oil/refined products (ISIC 4661 / NAICS 424720) without a Panama Hydrocarbons / Ministry of Energy license, or using a PIF to circumvent licensing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of USD 10,000 to USD 100,000, plus confiscation of profit from unlicensed operations. The DGI can disallow all deductions, yielding a 25% tax on gross receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The resident agent and PIF council members involved in unlicensed acts are jointly liable for restitution and fines; criminal penalties up to 3 years' imprisonment in serious cases.
